_comment: Single source of truth for every constant shared across modules or runtimes. Python reads it via crawlkit.contract; Node reads this exact file via node/lib/contract.js. tests/test_contract_parity.py fails if the two ever see different bytes.

user_agents.desktop_chrome: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/148.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
user_agents._comment: One registry. Copy-pasting this literal into each script that needs it is the obvious approach, and it drifts: seven copies end up at two different Chrome versions and nothing fails, because nothing compares them. Must never contain the token 'Headless' — crawlkit.ua.assert_no_headless_token() enforces that, because Chrome's new headless mode still emits it and it is the cheapest bot tell there is.

browser._comment: branded_chrome, not a bundled Chromium: Chromium-for-Testing leaks a different brand set and is fingerprinted. AutomationControlled clears navigator.webdriver. offscreen_window_position lets a real headful window (which passes far more checks than headless) run without stealing desktop focus.

exit_codes._comment: Both runtimes exit with these integers. Documenting a code is not producing one: sys.exit(<str>) prints to stderr and exits 1, so a renderer can promise 2 and 3 and deliver neither, leaving a caller unable to distinguish 'not installed' from 'render failed' from 'wall not cleared'. crawlkit.exits.die() writes the message to stderr and exits the integer.

http._comment: live_statuses is the set that ends the probe ladder without a GET fallback, and the set a sticky override must fall inside to be trusted. PDFs get the longer timeout because they are slow to first byte and a 10s cap turns a valid response into a false failure.

challenge._comment: Two predicates for one mechanism. title_pattern matches Cloudflare's interstitial <title>; min_body is the portable generalization — poll document.body.innerText.length, which survives the challenge's own auto-reload because the predicate re-evaluates in each new document. innerText, never innerHTML: a stub carries kilobytes of obfuscated script and almost no text. Never reload during the poll; a reload restarts the proof-of-work and can escalate to a hard block.

scroll._comment: Re-read document.body.scrollHeight on every iteration — it is the loop bound, so the loop extends as lazy content appends. Caching it is the classic refactor that silently truncates a harvest. The images preset fires more scroll events to trip more lazy image loads.

media._comment: hires_width is requested larger than anything the UI itself asks for, so the injected variant wins the largest-buffer-per-id comparison. drain_ms is required after the in-page injection resolves: CDP response events carrying the buffers arrive asynchronously on the Node side.

politeness._comment: Flat backoff, not exponential: 30s is long enough for a transient rate-flag to age out and keeps the worst case bounded. The inter-request sleep is jittered because a constant interval is itself a bot signature. attempt_timeout_s kills a hung browser whose own internal timeouts deadlocked.

gray_band._comment: A truncated JPEG still decodes; the undecoded remainder is flat mid-gray, so only pixel inspection catches it. Lower half only (truncation eats the bottom of a top-down encode). The mean AND variance conjunction is what spares a genuinely flat gray sky; 2-of-4 tolerates one legitimately flat band.

floors._comment: Two instances of one rule: a best match is not automatically a match. Below the floor the matcher returns nothing and the caller counts it, rather than forcing the nearest candidate.

sticky._comment: Written into a link-state record by a browser-grade confirmation; read by the cheap prober, which then skips the network entirely for that URL. Honored only in conjunction with a recorded status inside http.live_statuses, so a marker carrying a dead status is still re-probed.

vocabularies._comment: Closed vocabularies live here once. agents/verdicts.py validates against these values and agents/sections.py renders the in-prompt guide from the same object, filtered by offer_to_agent. That relation (prompt enum is a subset of accepted enum) is therefore structural rather than remembered: maintained as two separate lists, they skew, and the symptom is a whole fanout's worth of rejected records.

ok.gloss: page is live AND contains the claimed fact

wrong_topic.gloss: page is live but is the wrong material (generic landing page, prior-year data, different entity)

js_only.gloss: page is a JavaScript shell — no extractable content for a reader without JS

scanned_pdf.gloss: PDF whose text extraction yields nothing useful (image scan)

unverifiable.gloss: could not fetch: repeated timeouts, domain unreachable; mark and move on

ok.gloss: source rendered, items counted, the count is reliable

unparseable.gloss: image-scan PDF, JS shell, paywall, or otherwise not extractable (report a count of 0)

access_blocked.gloss: fetch failed: 403, 503, TLS error, repeated timeouts (report a count of 0)

manual.gloss: derived, never reported by an agent: the measurement could not be made, so coverage is unknown and is NOT scored as passing

undercoverage.gloss: derived: stored count is below the threshold fraction of the source count

uncertain.gloss: evidence is mixed or stale — return this plus the safest corrected statement

replace.gloss: a better source exists: return the new URL plus the evidence you saw on it

confirm_walled.gloss: the current URL is right but bot-walled: render it, and if the rendered page genuinely carries the fact, keep the URL

drop.gloss: no acceptable source exists anywhere on the owner's own site: say so in one sentence and the field is removed

fanout._comment: max_concurrent_agents is the observed safe band; more trips API rate limiting. emission_rule_width is the '=' rule framing one dispatchable prompt per block. marker is written into every emitted prompt and read back by recovery, so a dead agent's target is recovered from a machine-readable token rather than by regexing prose out of its prompt — and both runtimes must agree on it.

coverage._comment: The agent measures, the script judges. This number lives here and never reaches a prompt: an agent that knows what value passes will produce that value. Below the threshold is a real gap worth investigating; the tolerance above it absorbs legitimate declared exclusions.

locales._comment: A block page is written in the target's language, so matching one is language-specific by nature. Hardcoding a single language at module scope is wrong twice over: it fingerprints where the code was written, and it cannot be extended without editing the module. Default is English; CRAWLKIT_LOCALES=en,ru adds more. Every locale carries the same three categories (empty lists allowed) so a caller can enable one without discovering it is half-populated.
